sections.content:
Key finding! Transition 6:
- Action: MOUSE(row=51, col=15)
- Before: all gray
- After: 4 white cells in cross pattern
So clicking (51, 15) - which is in the LEFT PANEL - converted all cross cells to white!
This is the key. The left panel has the target pattern in purple. Clicking the left panel triggers the check and converts the cross cells to white.
So the mechanism is:
1. Click cells in the right panel to set them (gray <-> green toggle)
2. Click the left panel to trigger the check
3. If the green cells match the target pattern, check converts them to white
But wait, in transition 6, the before state was all gray, and the after state had 4 white cells. So clicking the left panel with all gray cells still converted them to white. This doesn't match the "check" hypothesis.
Actually, maybe clicking the left panel copies the left panel's pattern to the right panel. The left panel has 4 purple cells in cross pattern, and clicking it converts the right panel's cross cells to white.
But this seems too simple. Let me look at more transitions to understand the left panel's role.
Actually, looking at the coordinates, (51, 15) is in the left panel. The left panel is around row 49-59, col 10-20. So (51, 15) is in the left panel.
Let me look at what happens when clicking the left panel.
